newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NGC calls note holders' meeting.
newsitem.headline: NGC calls note holders' meeting.

text.p: Natural Gas Corp said on Tuesday it had called a meeting of capital note holders to consider modifying the terms by which notes are converted into shares.
The April 24 meeting will consider a proposed modification to the Trust Deed governing the notes which will make conversion fairer, the company said.
Chairman Mike Smith said it was proposed to modify a clause relating to the calculation of the market value of the company's ordinary shares for the purpose of the conversion of notes into shares.

If approved, the calculation of the weighted average of the share price would be based on all trades of the company's shares during the specified period of 15 consecutive trading days, rather than just the last reported trade on each of those days.

Smith said that given the potential for aberrations to influence the current narrow basis for calculation, the company believed the proposed amendment would deliver a fairer, more accurate assessment of the true market value of the shares for conversion purposes.
The convertible notes were issued for a fixed term of five years and conversion is scheduled for October 14 of this year.
Smith said the company as yet had made no decisions as to how the conversion would be effected.

"In seeking the modification to the Trust Deed at this time, the directors intentions are to ensure the mechanism they believe better serves the interests of all Note Holders is available should the need arise".
He added that the proposed modification had been discussed with the Trustee who considers it to be sensible.
